title: Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevina
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Chullin 99b: That man who came before Rabbi Chanina, and Rabbi Yehudah bar Zevina was sitting at the door. When he came out, Rabbi Yehuda asked him, "What did he say to you?" He said to him, "He permitted it to him." Rabbi Yehuda sent him back to Rabbi Chanina, who said, "Who is this who is troubling me? Go tell the one sitting at the door: sinews do not impart flavor." And in the Seder HaDorot (סה״ד) it says that Rabbi Yehudah bar Zevina — and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Chanina and Rav Yitzchak bar Chaluv, Chullin 99b. With all due respect, he mixed two matters together, for there it is a separate statement, as they say there afterwards: when they came before Rabbi Ami, he sent them before Rav Yitzchak bar Chaluv.

He is also mentioned in Sotah 12a, with several homilies from him, but it seems that one should read there, as in Berakhot 12b, Rabbi Yehudah bar Zevida; and in Dikdukei Soferim (דק״ס) the reading in Berakhot 12b and also in Bava Batra 102a is, in all of them, Rabbi Yehudah bar Zevina.

notes.text: Hyman distinguishes the questioner-at-the-door episode from the separate Rabbi Ami/Rav Yitzchak bar Chaluv statement. Zevida and Zevina are witness variants.
The notice gives Rav Yitzchak bar Chaluv; the checked William Davidson paragraph has Rabbi Yitzchak ben Chaluv. The different forms are preserved as witness readings.

The consulted Chullin 99b passage separates the questioner-at-the-door story from the subsequent Ami/Yitzchak ben Chaluv report. Hyman’s Rav/bar wording and Zevina/Zevida variants remain distinct from the consulted Rabbi/ben wording; his exact Dikdukei Soferim readings were not independently inspected.
